extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: MPEP guidance on processing replies after final Office actions, transitional after-final submissions (37 CFR 1.129(a)), examiner's amendments, extension-of-time practice (37 CFR 1.136), and Request for Continued Examination (RCE) practice (37 CFR 1.114).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing when PTOL-303 box 1.b is checked
rubrics_metrics.description: When box 1.b at the top portion of the Advisory Action form, PTOL-303, is checked, the time for applicant to take further action (including the calculation of extension fees under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) begins to run 3 months from the date of the final rejection, or from the date of the advisory action, whichever is later. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension fees cannot be prorated for portions of a month. Example: if applicant initially replies within 2 months and the examiner mails an advisory action before the end of 3 months, the shortened statutory period will expire at the end of 3 months from the date of mailing of the final rejection; if advisory mailed after the 3-month period, shortened statutory period expires on mailing date of advisory action and extension fees are calculated from that mailing date. See MPEP § 710.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment after complete first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, an examiner's amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without the payment of extension fees even if the examiner's amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action, as the application would be abandoned by operation of law at that point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for examiner's amendment when first reply not within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has not been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, applicant's authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3-month shortened statutory period or within an extended period for reply that has been petitioned and paid for by applicant pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's amendment correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final Office action would not require any extension fee because the reply put the application in condition for allowance except for correction of formal matters not previously required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time petition requirements (37 CFR 1.136(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee provided for in 37 CFR 1.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an extension is necessary to place an application in condition for allowance, applicant may file the petition and fee or give authorization to the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a deposit account. Office employees may not accept oral telephonic instructions to complete credit card payment or otherwise charge a patent process fee to a credit card. Authorization must be given before the extended period expires and must be of record in an examiner's amendment stating the person authorizing, when, deposit account number, length of extension requested, and amount to be charged. Form paragraph 13.02.02 should be used for telephone-authorized extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone authorization format for extension and examiner's amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 13.02.02 provides the required wording for recording a telephone authorization: identify date of call, person requesting extension, number of months requested, deposit account number, fee amount, and the examiner's amendment authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form notes that if changes are unacceptable, an amendment may be filed under 37 CFR 1.312 and that to ensure consideration the amendment must be submitted no later than payment of the issue fee. Examiner note refers to MPEP § 706.07(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of replies after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies should not be considered by the examiner unless filed within the shortened statutory period (SSP) or accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 37 CFR 1.136(a)). This requirement also applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply. See MPEP § 710.02(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be conducted after the expiration of the shortened statutory period for reply to a final Office action but within the 6-month statutory period for reply without the payment of an extension fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview practice is permitted in that window and does not, by itself, require payment of extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle practice for formal matters identified after reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply is made to a final Office action and which require action by applicant to correct may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No extension fees would be required since the reply put the application in condition for allowance except for the correction of formal matters which had not yet been required by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawing finality when reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid issue of abandonment and payment of extension fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: 'The finality of the Office action mailed is hereby withdrawn in view of the new ground of rejection set forth below.' Form paragraph 7.42 may be used. See MPEP § 706.07(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for transitional after-final practice (37 CFR 1.129(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in an application (not reissue or design) pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (taking into account earlier-filed application references under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c)) is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection if the first submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to filing an appeal brief and prior to abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee. A second submission is available under the same conditions if the application receives a subsequent final rejection. This transitional practice is only for applications filed on or before June 8, 1995 and not available for reissue, design, or reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance of submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' under 37 CFR 1.129(a) includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement (IDS), an amendment to the written description, claims or drawings, and a new substantive argument or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee may introduce new matter into the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132). Previously refused IDS may be treated as filed within allowed time periods if they comply with 37 CFR 1.98 and certain statement requirements. Examiners may introduce a new ground of rejection based on information submitted in the IDS and make the next Office action final, provided no other new ground of rejection (not necessitated by claim amendment) is introduced. See MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely payment of 37 CFR 1.17(r) fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon timely payment of the 37 CFR 1.17(r) fee, the finality of the previous Office action is withdrawn and previously unentered submissions (and submissions filed with the 1.17(r) fee) will be entered in the order in which they were filed, absent specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conflicting amendments exist, applicant should provide specific instructions for entry upon payment. Conditional payments (authorization to charge deposit account or credit card) will be treated as unconditional payment of the fee. Use form paragraph 7.42.01 to notify applicant that finality has been withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission treatment under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) is not fully responsive to the prior Office action, but appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS (whichever is longer) from the mailing date of the notice to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must set forth the reasons why the submission is not fully responsive. This shortened statutory period supersedes prior time periods and may be extended pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a). Payment of 1.17(r) with an appeal fee may be construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and continue prosecution under 1.129(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action-final possibility after a 1.129(a) submission filed prior to June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r) filed prior to June 8, 2005, the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.03 may be used to make such an action final. A shortened statutory period for reply to such a final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from mailing date; if first reply filed within TWO MONTHS and advisory action is mailed after end of three months, shortened statutory period expires on advisory mailing date. In no event will statutory period expire later than SIX MONTHS from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-June-8-2005 1.129(a) submission practice
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions and payment of the 1.17(r) fee on or after June 8, 2005, the next Office action on the merits is equivalent to the next Office action following a reply to a non-final Office action; under second-action-final practice, such an Office action will be made final except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is neither necessitated by applicant's amendment nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.031 may be used to make the next Office action final following a submission filed on or after June 8, 2005. The same shortened/maximum statutory period rules (3 months/6 months) apply and applicants are reminded of extension policy 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE statutory basis and general effect (35 U.S.C. 132; 37 CFR 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request continued examination (RCE) of an application by filing a submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of payment of the issue fee (unless petition under § 1.313 granted), abandonment, or filing of a notice of appeal/commencement of civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an RCE is timely filed, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action and the submission will be entered and considered. Filing an RCE after an appeal but prior to decision will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and to reopen prosecution before the examiner. An appeal brief/reply brief or related papers will not be considered a submission under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE inapplicability categories (37 CFR 1.114(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The RCE provisions do not apply to: (1) provisional applications; (2) utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before June 8, 1995; (3) international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 before June 8, 1995; (4) design patent applications; or (5) patents under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.114(e) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE submission content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' for RCE purposes includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of § 1.111. A previously filed amendment after final (whether or not entered) may satisfy the submission requirement. Previously filed appeal or reply brief arguments may be incorporated by reference or copied into the submission. Arguments entered after final but not found persuasive may satisfy the submission if they are responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE cannot be used to 'switch inventions' (independent and distinct claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot file an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions). Any newly submitted claims directed to an invention independent and distinct from the previously claimed invention will be withdrawn from consideration and not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.145 and related MPEP discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE is not a new application; no conversion to CPA or new application
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE is not the filing of a new application; the Office will not convert an RCE to a new application such as an application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) or a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RCE process reopens prosecution in the same application; applicants seeking a new application/CPA must use the appropriate continuing-application filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing verification for RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE will be initially processed by the Technology Center assigned the application; technical support personnel will verify that the RCE included a submission as required by 37 CFR 1.114(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent processing steps depend on status of application (after final, after allowance, after appeal, after Ex parte Quayle, etc.). See subsections V–XII for specific status-dependent processing requirements.
